messages:
maria: quick sync — we're planning the tenant-subnet migration (peering -> private endpoint) next week, goal: zero-downtime for live customers. sharing the proposed canary steps.
raj: sounds good. are we assuming customers already have route to the private endpoint eni? or do we create an elastic interface during cutover?
kai: plan A was ephemeral ENI created in customer subnet + add route to it in tenant route table, remove peering. plan B is keep peering as hot fallback and shift traffic via DNS first.
maria: right — tradeoff is cost/complexity. ephemeral ENI + route swap is cleaner but involves IAM + automation in customer's VPC. DNS shift easier but TTLs and split-brain risk if route still points to peering.
linh: question: how will health checking work during transition? if we DNS failover to private endpoint but ENI isn't fully ready we might blackhole.
aj: propose step 0: verify path via one-off test instance in tenant subnet hitting private endpoint IP. step 1: create ENI + attach, run e2e healthcheck from inside tenant (script below). step 2: if green, update route to point to ENI. step 3: monitor for 15m, then detach peering.
kai: what's the healthcheck script? can we reuse the existing agent-checker?
linh: small snippet: `curl -sS -m 3 http://10.0.4.5:8080/healthz || exit 1` plus token auth. Also check TLS handshake for mutual certs.
maria: 👍 also keep peering route as fallback for 30m via route priority: set route to ENI with longer prefix length? aws doesn't support priority on same prefix. alternative: adjust route tables atomically: add ENI route then remove peering.
raj: add a monitoring gate: `sum(infra.request_success{route:eni} by (tenant) > 0 and request_latency_p50{route:eni} < 300)` for canary. if gate fails rollback to peering.
linh: DNS TTL note — if we rely on DNS we need TTL 30s minimum and ensure resolver caches in-app honorring low TTL. many customers' resolvers ignore short TTLs.
kai: ops-bot: schedule automation job for canary tenant list and runbook link
devops-bot: scheduled job created: job-id=job-57924-tenant-mig, runs 2026-03-25T02:00:00Z, notifies #eng-oncall on failures
maria: onboarding runbook outline (short):
- precheck: IAM perms, subnet free IP, agent cert present
- create ENI (tag tenant+job)
- run health checks from inside tenant
- swap route to ENI
- monitor metrics & logs for 30m
- remove peering & clean up ENI
- post-check: reconciliation and audit event
raj: rollback plan: if errors in 5m window, recreate peering route (we never delete peering until step final), or change app DNS back if we used DNS. also revert ENI route.
linh: can we do partial canary by prefixing specific tenant IP ranges? some customers have stretched subnets; route granularity may be messy.
kai: suggestion: start with smallest, single-tenant accounts or internal beta tenants. test multiple AZ failure scenarios too (ENI freeze, AZ failover).
maria: agreed. owners: @raj handles automation, @linh health checks, @kai monitoring dashboards. I'll draft runbook and a tiny terraform module for ENI lifecycle.
raj: I'll open PR for automation and add a dry-run feature.
maria: thanks — sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to lock schedule. :thumbsup:
